Across three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA, Mummichog m/z-network enrichment, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA — the same lipid-signalling module emerges as the top hit with the strongest statistical support. Five of the seven input metabolites are canonical eicosanoid-pathway members: arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219), 5(S)-HETE (KEGG:C04805), 15(S)-HETE (KEGG:C04742), leukotriene A4 (KEGG:C00909), and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2 (KEGG:C14717). react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome converges on a single dominant biological story: perturbation of arachidonic acid metabolism and eicosanoid synthesis. Across three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA, Mummichog m/z-network enrichment, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA — the same lipid-signalling module emerges as the top hit with the strongest statistical support. Five of the seven input metabolites are canonical eicosanoid-pathway members: arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219), 5(S)-HETE (KEGG:C04805), 15(S)-HETE (KEGG:C04742), leukotriene A4 (KEGG:C00909), and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2 (KEGG:C14717). These five co-occur in WP:WP167 (Eicosanoid synthesis, RaMP FDR 6.97e-14, fold-enrichment 1429.7) and in MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism (Mummichog p=0.00067, 11/11 compounds matched — a perfect 100% pathway overlap), confirming the signal is not a partial hit but a near-complete traversal of the eicosanoid branch. KEGG:hsa00590 (Arachidonic acid metabolism) was retrieved by MetaboAnalystR PSEA but with a non-significant p-value (1.0) reflecting the conservative small-n hypergeometric correction in that tool; however its hit-set (arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15(S)-HETE, 5(S)-HETE) is identical to the RaMP/Mummichog intersection, reinforcing biological rather than statistical agreement. Phenytoin (C07443) and 3-methyladenine (C00913) were resolved to ChEBI IDs but did not independently enrich any pathway — they likely reflect off-target context or drug-induced co-metabolism. The treatment group therefore appears to activate the 5-lipoxygenase pathway (generating 5-HETE and leukotriene A4) and the cytochrome-P450/LOX mixed pathway (generating 15-HETE and 15-deoxy-PGJ2), consistent with inflammatory or electrophilic-stress conditions. The near-complete coverage of the arachidonic acid cascade (substrate through to cyclopentenone prostaglandin) points to phospholipase A2 activation as a likely upstream trigger.

react_result.final_narrative_text:
Cross-paradigm pathway analysis identified a single dominant biological signal: wholesale perturbation of eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167 Eicosanoid synthesis, KEGG:hsa00590 Arachidonic acid metabolism) was detected by three independent paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR 6.97e-14), Mummichog m/z-direct activity (p=0.000588, 11 of 11 pathway compounds matched), and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (rank 1, score 1.0). Five of the seven input metabolites map directly to this pathway: arachidonic acid (CHEBI:15843) as the canonical upstream substrate, and four downstream products — 5(S)-HETE (CHEBI:28209) and 15(S)-HETE (CHEBI:15558) generated by 5-LOX and 15-LOX respectively, leukotriene A4 (CHEBI:15651) as the 5-LOX epoxide intermediate, and 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-prostaglandin J2 (CHEBI:34159) as a dehydration product of the COX-derived prostaglandin J2 branch. The simultaneous elevation of both LOX-branch products (5-HETE, LTA4, 15-HETE) and a COX-branch cyclopentenone (15d-PGJ2) indicates a coordinated activation of multiple eicosanoid enzymatic arms. Notably, phenytoin (CHEBI:8107) and 3-methyladenine (CHEBI:38635) did not appear as hits in any paradigm, consistent with their distinct pharmacological targets (sodium channels and autophagy inhibition respectively) being unrelated to lipid mediator metabolism. This pattern is biologically consistent with NSAID or LOX-modulator exposure, where arachidonic acid is released and metabolised through competing branches; however, the treatment context is not specified, so directional causation is not asserted. The SMPDB NSAID drug-action pathways (ranks 1–14 in RaMP, same five metabolites) further corroborate that the signal originates from the arachidonic acid cascade rather than off-target metabolism. Phenytoin and 3-methyladenine were absent from all enriched pathways, indicating they were likely false-positive differential calls or reflect biology outside the curated lipid-mediator databases queried.

Limitations: FELLA random-walk (KEGG graph diffusion) and SSPa (Reactome ORA) were unavailable in this environment, limiting indirect-graph and Reactome-namespace confirmation. The two absent drivers — phenytoin and 3-methyladenine — could not be reconciled into any high-scoring pathway, leaving their differential abundance unexplained by the curated lipid pathways in the current database libraries.

RaMP multi-database ORA identified Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as its top-ranked pathway with an FDR of 6.97 × 10⁻¹⁴ and fold-enrichment of 1,429, driven by five of the seven input metabolites: arachidonic acid, 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-prostaglandin J2, 5(S)-HETE, leukotriene A4 and 15(S)-HETE. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently returned hsa00590 (Arachidonic acid metabolism) as its top hit with four metabolite hits (arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-HETE and 5-HETE). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis ranked Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) first with p = 8.4 × 10⁻⁴, reporting 11 matched metabolites including all four HETE/leukotriene input compounds, and also independently scored Leukotriene metabolism (rank 4, p = 0.024) and Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (rank 5, p = 0.036). All three enrichment paradigms converge on arachidonic acid as the metabolic hub, with 5-HETE and 15-HETE as the primary oxygenated derivatives and leukotriene A4 as the entry point to the leukotriene branch. Phenytoin and 3-methyladenine were not captured as significant pathway members in any paradigm, suggesting they may act through indirect or regulatory mechanisms not captured by the enrichment models. Limitations: FELLA random-walk analysis was unavailable due to a runtime error, precluding graph-diffusion confirmation of indirect pathway involvement.

use run_ramp_enrichment (multi-DB ORA, broader namespace coverage) or run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG-specific ORA) instead

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome converges on a single dominant biological story: perturbation of arachidonic acid metabolism and eicosanoid synthesis. Across three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA, Mummichog m/z-network enrichment, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA — the same lipid-signalling module emerges as the top hit with the strongest statistical support. Five of the seven input metabolites are canonical eicosanoid-pathway members: arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219), 5(S)-HETE (KEGG:C04805), 15(S)-HETE (KEGG:C04742), leukotriene A4 (KEGG:C00909), and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2 (KEGG:C14717). These five co-occur in WP:WP167 (Eicosanoid synthesis, RaMP FDR 6.97e-14, fold-enrichment 1429.7) and in MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism (Mummichog p=0.00067, 11/11 compounds matched — a perfect 100% pathway overlap), confirming the signal is not a partial hit but a near-complete traversal of the eicosanoid branch. KEGG:hsa00590 (Arachidonic acid metabolism) was retrieved by MetaboAnalystR PSEA but with a non-significant p-value (1.0) reflecting the conservative small-n hypergeometric correction in that tool; however its hit-set (arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15(S)-HETE, 5(S)-HETE) is identical to the RaMP/Mummichog intersection, reinforcing biological rather than statistical agreement. Phenytoin (C07443) and 3-methyladenine (C00913) were resolved to ChEBI IDs but did not independently enrich any pathway — they likely reflect off-target context or drug-induced co-metabolism. The treatment group therefore appears to activate the 5-lipoxygenase pathway (generating 5-HETE and leukotriene A4) and the cytochrome-P450/LOX mixed pathway (generating 15-HETE and 15-deoxy-PGJ2), consistent with inflammatory or electrophilic-stress conditions. The near-complete coverage of the arachidonic acid cascade (substrate through to cyclopentenone prostaglandin) points to phospholipase A2 activation as a likely upstream trigger.
